# 2 Baruch Chapter 54 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Cloud and Waters Vision

---

**1** Then I woke up and got up and prayed:

**2** "O Lord, you show me so much and teach me so many things, but now you have shown me something I cannot understand.

**3** The vision was partly comforting and partly troubling — I have seen things I cannot explain.

**4** "So I beg you, O Lord my God, to explain this vision to me.

**5** I know that you showed me the earlier things I asked about;

**6** now I ask you to show me the meaning of this vision as well.

**7** "For at the end of the age, punishment will come to the wicked, and a new world will be opened up for the righteous.

**8** We have not yet received that world because we have not yet been found worthy of it;

**9** but because we have suffered so much in this world, we have been made worthy of the world to come.

**10** "No one can know all the things that belong to that coming world.

**11** This world was not created for humanity's sake — it is the coming world that was prepared for humanity.

**12** This world is nothing but trouble and weariness and hard labor for people; but the coming world will be a crown of great glory.

**13** "So, Lord, I am crying out to you. Please do not let my sin and wrongdoing overpower me;

**14** keep me in mind before you, and do not let human deeds hold sway over me.

**15** From the very beginning I have been your servant and devoted myself to serving you.

**16** "Now I beg you, O Lord God: let your mercy cover us generously. Do not deal with us according to what we have done,

**17** but according to your loving-kindness.

**18** "If you repay us according to our deeds, we have no response to give you.

**19** What are we, after all, that we should speak to you? We are nothing but dust before you.

**20** O Lord our God, save us for the sake of your name.

**21** "You made us, and you have mercy on those you have made. You do not abandon your own creatures.

**22** Every human being who has ever been born has sinned — but you, O Lord, forgive them and have mercy on them."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Prioritizes clarity and natural English flow while preserving the theological and narrative content of the Syriac source.*
